summary: Cambodia issues a 30-day tourist eVisa online (30 USD) and a 30 USD visa on arrival to most nationalities, while ASEAN neighbors enter visa-free. All arrivals are asked to complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before travel.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Cambodia

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage with evacuation is strongly recommended — serious cases are often treated in Bangkok or Singapore.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Cambodia

onwardTicket.text: Onward travel is rarely checked by Cambodian immigration, but airlines may still ask for it at check-in — having a booking avoids problems.

declarations.name: Cambodia e-Arrival Card (CeA)
declarations.text: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one free online form (web or CeA mobile app), submitted within 7 days before arrival. It has replaced the paper forms at the international airports; enforcement at land borders is still uneven — complete it in advance to be safe.

source.name: Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA)

currencyLimits.text: Cash of 10,000 USD or more (or equivalent) must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Cambodia

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and up to 2 liters of alcohol per adult.
The customs declaration is part of the Cambodia e-Arrival form.

payments.text: Cambodia runs on cash, and US dollars circulate alongside the riel. Prices are often quoted in USD, with riel used for small change. Bring crisp, undamaged USD notes (torn bills are refused). Cards work only in upmarket hotels and restaurants.

safety.text: Cambodia is generally safe for visitors. Watch for bag-snatching in Phnom Penh, and be alert to scams around border crossings and organized-fraud compounds advertised as jobs. Stick to marked paths in remote areas — landmines remain a risk off-road in some provinces.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Cambodia travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cool, dry season — ideal for Angkor and the coast. March to May is very hot; June to October brings monsoon rains.

idp.text: Cambodia is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Apply for the eVisa only at the official evisa.gov.kh — lookalike sites charge inflated fees for the same 30 USD visa or sell fakes.

At land crossings (especially Poipet from Thailand), touts and even officials may demand extra "fees". The visa on arrival costs 30 USD flat. Pay in USD, refuse baht "conversions", and consider getting the eVisa beforehand.
Carry small-denomination, crisp US dollar bills. Damaged or old-series notes are widely refused; change under 1 USD comes back in riel.
The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free — complete it at arrival.gov.kh or the official CeA app within 7 days before travel, and ignore paid third-party sites.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Cambodia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD in cash) at airports and major land borders. Both allow a 30-day stay, extendable once by 30 days.

faq.question: Is the Cambodia eVisa better than the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: They cost the same (30 USD online or at the border) and both give 30 days. The eVisa skips the arrival line and avoids border overcharging, but it is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Trapeang Kriel land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.

faq.question: What is the Cambodia e-Arrival card?
faq.answer: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the CeA app. It replaces the paper arrival forms at the international airports.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Cambodia?
faq.answer: A tourist (T) visa can be extended once by 30 days at the immigration department or through agents. For longer stays, enter on an ordinary (E-class) visa instead. It can be extended in-country for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.

faq.question: Which nationalities enter Cambodia visa-free?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEAN countries enter visa-free: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt. Nearly everyone else needs the eVisa or a visa on arrival.
